column3: “My standing was” is rendered “I arose,” and “strengthener” “encouragement.”
“Wealth” is rendered “riches”; NASB renders “according to his strength by his riches” as “as soon as he becomes strong through his riches,” and “kingdom” as “realm.”
“Dominion” is rendered “authority.”
“The four winds of the heavens” is rendered “the four points of the compass”; NASB adds “given.”
“Commanders” is rendered “princes”; NASB adds “who will gain ascendancy” and “indeed.”
“Uprightnesses” is rendered “a peaceful arrangement,” “the power of the arm” “her position of power,” and “fathered” “sired.”
“One of the shoot of her roots” is rendered “one of the descendants of her line”; “prevail” is rendered “display great strength.”
“Vessels of their desire” is rendered “precious vessels,” and “molten images” “metal images”; NASB renders “stand away from” as “refrain from attacking.”
NASB supplies “the latter” for the subject.
“Certainly go” is rendered “keep on coming”; NASB supplies “one of them.”
NASB supplies “the latter” and “the former” to identify the kings.
Close to the Hebrew.
“At the end of the times, years” is rendered “after an interval of some years.”
“The sons of the violent ones” is rendered “the violent ones”; “stumble” is rendered “fall down.”
“A city of fortifications” is rendered “a well-fortified city”; “the people of his choicest ones” is rendered “not even their choicest troops.”
NASB adds “for a time”; “complete destruction” is rendered “destruction.”
“Upright things with him” is rendered “bringing with him a proposal of peace”; NASB renders “not to him it will happen” as “or be on his side.” The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
“For him” is rendered “against him”; “not his scorn he will turn back to him” is rendered “moreover, he will repay him for his scorn.” The meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew.
“The splendor of a kingdom” is rendered “the Jewel of his kingdom,” and “days one” “a few days.”
“Royalty” is rendered “kingship” and “the kingdom”; “in quietness” is rendered “in a time of tranquility.”
“The forces of the flood” is rendered “the overflowing forces.”
“With fewness of a nation” is rendered “with a small force of people.”
“In quietness” is rendered “In a time of tranquility,” and “fertile places of the province” “richest parts of the realm”; NASB adds “only.”
“Heart” is rendered “courage”; “people will plan plans” is rendered “schemes will be devised.”
“Break him” is rendered “destroy him”; NASB adds “but.”
NASB adds “to each other.”
“Property” is rendered “plunder.”
NASB adds “this last time” and renders the comparison as “the way it did before.”
“Pay attention to” is rendered “show regard for”; “direct indignation” is rendered “become enraged.”
